title: Temurah 32
description: The mishna on rules shared by altar and Temple-maintenance consecration, the refutation of Rav Huna on dedicating altar offerings to the priests, Ulla on a burnt offering consecrated for Temple maintenance and its two counts of misuse, and Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish on which consecrated animals that died must be buried.
topics: 🔒 Mishna: no moving one sanctity to another, yet a consecration of value and a dedication take effect
⚔️ Rav Huna: altar offerings dedicated to the priests? Nothing. Two baraitot refute him
📖 “Every dedicated item is most holy”: Rav Huna’s verse and Ulla’s reading
🐂 Ulla: a burnt offering consecrated for Temple maintenance has only the treasurers’ delay; the rest is rabbinic
⚖️ Misuse: Rabbi Yannai, Rabbi’s “all the fat is the Lord’s,” and the two counts of misuse
🪦 Died before redemption: buried or redeemed? Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish on standing and valuation
📜 A baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan: “of which they may not bring an offering”

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֵין מְשַׁנִּין אוֹתָן מִקְּדוּשָּׁה לִקְדוּשָּׁה, וּמַקְדִּישִׁין אוֹתָן הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִילּוּי, וּמַחְרִימִין אוֹתָן, וְאִם מֵתוּ — יִקָּבֵרוּ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אִם מֵתוּ — יִפָּדוּ.

a2.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁהִתְפִּיסָן לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים — לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר קְרָא: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״ — כׇּל חֵרֶם דְּקֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הָוֵי, הָהוּא לַה׳ לֶיהֱוֵי.

a3.he: מֵיתִיבִי: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת שֶׁהִתְפִּיסָן, בֵּין לְקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ בֵּין לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים — לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם.

a4.he: חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים שֶׁהִתְפִּיסָן, בֵּין לְקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, בֵּין לְקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם.

a5.he: הָא קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁהִתְפִּיס לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא!

a6.he: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: כִּי שַׁיְּירַהּ — אַהָדָא שַׁיְּירַהּ, דְּקָדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁהִתְפִּיסָן לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי, אֲבָל לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים — לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם.

a7.he: וְלִיתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי הָנָךְ! תַּנָּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי — קָתָנֵי, דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי — לָא קָתָנֵי.

a8.he: תְּנַן: ״מַקְדִּישׁ אוֹתָן הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִילּוּי״, מַאי לַָאו ״הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִילּוּי״ — לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, וּ״מַחְרִימִין״ — לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֵן?

a9.he: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְלָא שְׁנָא מַפֵּיק לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן ״הַקֹּדֶשׁ״ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְלָא שְׁנָא מַפֵּיק לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן ״(חֶרְמֵי) [חֵרֶם]״ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a10.he: וְהָא לָא תָּנֵי הָכִי, דְּתַנְיָא בְּבָרַיְיתָא: הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִילּוּי — קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, מַחְרִימִין אוֹתָם — חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים! וְעוֹד, הָא תַּנְיָא: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁן לְחֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי! תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא, תְּיוּבְתָּא.

a11.he: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא קְרָא קָאָמַר! אָמַר עוּלָּא: אָמַר קְרָא ״חֵרֶם כׇּל חֵרֶם״.

a12.he: וּמִי אָמַר עוּלָּא הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר עוּלָּא: הַמַּתְפִּיס עוֹלָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת — אֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא עִיכּוּב

b3.he: לִמְעִילָה לְמָה לֵיהּ קְרָא? קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ!

b4.he: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵין מְעִילָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת מִן הַתּוֹרָה אֶלָּא בְּעוֹלָה בִּלְבָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִמְעוֹל מַעַל וְחָטְאָה בִּשְׁגָגָה מִקׇּדְשֵׁי ה׳״, הַמְיוּחָדִין לַה׳. אֲבָל חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם לָא נָפְקָא אֶלָּא מִדְּרַבִּי.

b5.he: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב לַה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֵימוּרֵי קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים לִמְעִילָה.

b6.he: לְמָה לִי קְרָא? ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ! אֶלָּא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ, בָּעֵי קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיִינְהוּ לִמְעִילָה. חֲרָמִים נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ, בָּעֵי קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיִינְהוּ לִמְעִילָה.

b7.he: גּוּפָא: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ עוֹלָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת — אֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא עִיכּוּב גִּיזְבָּרִין בִּלְבַד. מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ עוֹלָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת — אָסוּר לְשׁוֹחֳטָהּ עַד שֶׁתִּפָּדֶה!

b8.he: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: אִם עָבַר וּשְׁחָטָהּ — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי.

b9.he: אֶלָּא מַאי מִדְּרַבָּנַן? אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וּמוֹעֲלִין שְׁתֵּי מְעִילוֹת, וְאִי מִדְּרַבָּנַן — אַמַּאי שְׁתֵּי מְעִילוֹת? הָכִי קָאָמַר: וּרְאוּיָה לִמְעוֹל בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי מְעִילוֹת.

b11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבָּנַן: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.

b12.he: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְרַבָּנַן, קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.

b13.he: וְזֶה וָזֶה, מוֹדֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וְקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל, בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ לֹא הָיָה בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.

b14.he: תְּנַן: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת שֶׁמֵּתוּ יִפָּדוּ״. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר לְרַבָּנַן אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, הַיְינוּ דְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְפָרוֹשֵׁי ״קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת שֶׁמֵּתוּ יִפָּדוּ״.

b15.he: אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, לְמָה לֵיהּ לְפָרוֹשֵׁי? לֵימָא ״אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ״!

b16.he: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי דְּאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ — מוֹדֵינָא לָךְ, בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ.

b17.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״אִם בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה״ — בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁיִּפָּדוּ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.

b18.he: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אִם בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ״ — הֲרֵי בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אָמוּר,

messages.text: 31b closed the Gemara on the previous mishna with the by-products of consecrated animals: one who derives benefit from milk of sacrificial animals or eggs of pigeons consecrated for the altar is not liable for misuse. A new mishna begins.
Mishna
With regard to both animals consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance, one may not alter their designation from one form of sanctity to another form of sanctity.
messages.lead: While the previous mishna enumerated differences between consecration for the altar and consecration for Temple maintenance, this mishna enumerates halakhot that apply to both.

notes.he: דקדשי בדק הבית שהקדישם למזבח לא עשה כלום ובקדשי מזבח אין משנין מקדושת עולה לשלמים ומשלמים לעולה:
notes.en: Mishna. From sanctity to sanctity: items consecrated for Temple maintenance that one consecrated for the altar, he has done nothing. And with items consecrated for the altar, one does not alter them from the sanctity of a burnt offering to a peace offering, or from a peace offering to a burnt offering.

notes.he: אין משנין אותן מקדושה לקדושה ולא אפי' מקדושה קלה לקדושה חמורה כגון שלמים לעולה:
notes.en: One may not alter them from one sanctity to another: and not even from a lighter sanctity to a more stringent sanctity, for example from a peace offering to a burnt offering.

messages.text: But one may consecrate animals already consecrated for the altar by a consecration of their value, and that value is donated to the Temple treasury for maintenance.

notes.he: אקדשי מזבח קאי:
notes.en: And one may consecrate them: this refers to items consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: כגון אם אמר על עולה הרי זו לבדק הבית מעלין אותה בדמים לפי מה שיש לו כח בה ונותן לגזבר דתנן בערכין בפ' המקדיש (ערכין דף כח:) מחרים אדם את קדשיו אם נדר נותן דמיהם ואם נדבה נותן את טובתם כלומר אם בהמה זו היתה נדר כגון דאמר הרי עלי עולה והפריש זו לנדרו כיון דאם מתה או נגנבה חייב באחריותה נמצא שכולה שלו ונותן כל דמיה לחרם הכהן והוא הדין נמי לבדק הבית אם התפיס קדשי מזבח לבדק הבית ואם נדבה דאם מתה אינו חייב באחריותה נמצא שאין לו חלק בה אלא טובת הנאה דרשאי ליטול דבר מועט מישראל חבירו כדי שיתן עולתו זאת לבן בתו כהן להקריבה כדי שיטול את העור וכפי אותה טובת הנאה יתן לבדק הבית:
notes.en: A consecration of value: for example, if he said of a burnt offering, “This is hereby for Temple maintenance,” it is appraised in money according to the share he has in it, and he gives [that sum] to the treasurer. As we learned in Arakhin, in the chapter HaMakdish (Arakhin 28b): A person may dedicate his consecrated items; if it was a vow, he gives their value, and if it was a gift-offering, he gives their benefit. That is to say: if this animal was a vow, for example he said, “It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering,” and set this one aside for his vow, then since he bears responsibility for it if it dies or is stolen, it turns out that it is wholly his, and he gives its entire value to the priest’s dedication. And the same holds for Temple maintenance, if he associated items consecrated for the altar with Temple maintenance. And if it was a gift-offering, then since he bears no responsibility for it if it dies, it turns out that he has no share in it except the benefit of discretion: he is allowed to take a small sum from a fellow Israelite in exchange for giving this burnt offering of his to [the Israelite’s] daughter’s son, a priest, to sacrifice it, so that he may take the hide. And according to that benefit of discretion he gives to Temple maintenance.

notes.he: לשון שומא כמו מעלין בדמים כלומר שמין כמה כח יש לו בה כדמפרש בערכין (דף כח:) המתפיס עולה לבדק הבית אם נדר נותן את דמיה שהרי אם היה נאבד היה חייב לשלם ואם נדבה נותן לפי טובת הנאה שבה פי' ומצי שקיל דבר מועט מישראל חברו כדי להקריב במשמר בן בתו כהן לשון רש"י ול"נ דלא מצינו זה הלשון דליתב לבן בתו כהן כ"א גבי בכור (בכורות דף כז.) לכן נראה לפרש כדתנן בהדיא בערכין (גם זה שם) ואם נדבה אומדין כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בשור זה לעולה ואע"פ שאינו רשאי פי' אע"פ שאינו חייב כמו (חולין דף נד:) אין בעלי אומנין רשאין לעמוד פי' חייבין ובערכין (גם זה שם) מפיק הקדש עילוי מדכתיב כל חרם קדש קדשים מלמד שהחרם חל אקדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים והקדש עילוי אקדשי מזבח קאי דאי אקדשי בדק הבית אמר בגמרא דקדשי בדק הבית שהקדיש לקדשי מזבח לחרמי כהנים לא עשה ולא כלום ופירש"י בגמרא דלא שייך טובת הנאה בקדשי בדק הבית ולא נהירא למורי האי טעמא דאטו מי לא שייך ביה לומר כמה אדם רוצה ליתן לבדק הבית אע"פ שאינו רשאי כמו בקדשי מזבח ונראה למורי דטעמא משום דבקדשי מזבח יש שם הבעלים לפדותן כשהוממו אבל בקדשי בדק הבית שהקדישן אין לבעלים עליהן יותר משאר אדם לפיכך אין בידו להתפיס:
notes.en: In brief: Hekdesh ilui is a term of appraisal, like “they raise it in money”: one assesses how much of a share he has in the animal, as Arakhin (28b) explains of one who associates a burnt offering with Temple maintenance: if it was a vow he gives its value, since had it been lost he would have had to pay; if a gift-offering, he gives according to the benefit of discretion in it. Rashi explains that benefit as a small sum a fellow Israelite would pay to have it offered in the watch of his daughter’s son, a priest. Tosafot object that this expression is found only regarding the firstborn (Bekhorot 27a), and prefer what Arakhin teaches explicitly: with a gift-offering, one assesses how much a person would want to give for this ox to offer it as a burnt offering, even though he is not “permitted,” meaning not obligated (as “craftsmen are not permitted to stand,” Ḥullin 54b). Arakhin derives the consecration of value from “every dedicated item is most holy”: a dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and on offerings of lesser sanctity. The consecration of value refers to items consecrated for the altar, since the Gemara says that items consecrated for Temple maintenance associated with the altar or with the priests’ dedications are nothing. Rashi’s reason there, that the benefit of discretion does not apply to them, did not satisfy Tosafot’s teacher, since one could ask of them too how much a person would want to give; rather, with items consecrated for the altar the owner has a standing to redeem them once they become blemished, while with items he consecrated for Temple maintenance he has no more claim than anyone else, so it is not in his power to associate them. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: פירוש לקדשי מזבח:
notes.en: And one may consecrate them: meaning, items consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: לשם קדשי בדה"ב ואותו עילוי נותן לבד"ה ומהו עילוי כדאמרינן בערכין בפרק המקדיש שדהו אם נדר שאמר שור זה עלי לעולה שחייב באחריותו כיון דלא סגי דלא מקריב ליה דחייב באחריותו נותן את דמיו לבדק הבית הואיל והקדישו הקדש עילוי לבדק הבית ואם נדבה היא אותו קדשי מזבח שהקדיש לעילוי כיון דנדבה דלא אמר עלי אלא הרי זו עולה דלא חייב באחריותה אינו נותן לבדק הבית אלא דמי טובת הנאתה ומה הוא טובתה (אומרין במה) [אומדים כמה] אדם כהן (אחד) [אחר] שאינו ממשמר העובד באותו זמן רוצה ליתן לבעלים של השור בשור זה שימתין לו עד זמן משמרתו ויתנהו לו להעלותו עולה כדי שיזכה בעורו שאינו רשאי זה כהן להעלותו אלא בזמן משמרתו וכמה שאותו כהן רוצה ליתן לו כן הוא ליתן לבדק הבית והיינו עילוי:
notes.en: A consecration of value: for the sake of items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and that value he gives to Temple maintenance. And what is the value? As we say in Arakhin, in the chapter HaMakdish Sadehu: if it was a vow, that he said, “This ox is incumbent upon me as a burnt offering,” he bears responsibility for it, since he cannot avoid sacrificing it; and since he bears responsibility for it, he gives its value to Temple maintenance, since he consecrated it with a consecration of value for Temple maintenance. And if that item consecrated for the altar which he consecrated for its value was a gift-offering, where he did not say “incumbent upon me” but “This is hereby a burnt offering,” so that he does not bear responsibility for it, he gives to Temple maintenance only the value of its benefit. And what is its benefit? One assesses how much another priest, who is not of the watch serving at that time, would want to give the owner of the ox for this ox, so that he wait for him until the time of his watch and give it to him to offer as a burnt offering, so that he may acquire its hide; for this priest is not permitted to offer it except in the time of his watch. And as much as that priest would want to give him, that is what he gives to Temple maintenance; and this is the value.

messages.text: And one may dedicate them for the purpose of giving their value to the priests.

notes.he: אם החרים קדשי מזבח נותן לכהן העילוי כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: And one may dedicate them: if he dedicated items consecrated for the altar, he gives the priest the value, as I explained.

notes.he: קדשי מזבח יכול לומר יהו חרם ואם כן אם נדר הם נותן את דמיהן לכהנים ואם נדבה נותן את טובתו כדאמרן:
notes.en: And one may dedicate them: items consecrated for the altar; he may say, “Let them be a dedication.” And if so, if they are a vow, he gives their value to the priests, and if a gift-offering, he gives its benefit, as we said.

messages.text: And if animals consecrated either for the altar or for Temple maintenance died, they must be buried.

notes.he: קדשי מזבח אפי' לאחר שהוממו אבל עדיין לא נפדו יקברו ואינו יכול לפדותם ולהאכילן לכלבים ואפילו למאן דאמר פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים הני מילי בשנעשו טרפה דאיכא העמדה והערכה אבל מתו לא דבעינן העמדה והערכה. אי נמי האי מתו כגון שעבר ושחטם קודם פדיונן וקאמר דשוב אינו יכול לפדותן ולאוכלן דבעינן העמדה והערכה ויקברו:
notes.en: If they died: items consecrated for the altar, even after they became blemished, but were not yet redeemed, are buried; he cannot redeem them and feed them to the dogs. And even according to the one who says that one may redeem consecrated animals to feed them to the dogs, that applies when they became tereifa, where standing and valuation is still possible; but if they died, not, since we require standing and valuation. Alternatively, this “died” is, for example, where he transgressed and slaughtered them before their redemption, and it says that he can no longer redeem them and eat them, since we require standing and valuation; and they are buried.

messages.text: Although that is the halakha with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, if animals consecrated for Temple maintenance died, they can be redeemed.

notes.he: דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה כדמוכח טעמא בגמרא:
notes.en: They can be redeemed: because they were not included in [the halakha of] standing and valuation, as the reason is shown in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara

With regard to animals consecrated for the altar, if one associated such objects of his vow with dedications for the priests, i.e., he vowed to give their value as a dedication to the priests, he has done nothing.

notes.he: היינו סתם חרמין. ולהכי נקט לשון חרמי כהנים דזימנין דחרמים לבדק הבית כגון אי פריש ואמר הרי זה חרם לבדק הבית:
notes.en: Gemara. Dedications to priests: these are unspecified dedications. And he used the expression “dedications to priests” because sometimes dedications are for Temple maintenance, for example if he specified and said, “This is hereby a dedication for Temple maintenance.”

notes.he: ואפי' הקדש עילוי לא יהיב לכהנים:
notes.en: He has done nothing: and he does not give the priests even the consecration of value.

notes.dh: קדשי מזבח שהתפיסן לחרמי כהנים שאמר יהו חרם לא אמר כלום
notes.he: ואינו נותן לכהנים לא דמיהן ולא טובתן:
notes.en: Items consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests, saying, “Let them be a dedication”: he has said nothing, and he gives the priests neither their value nor their benefit.

messages.text: What is the reason?

The verse states: “Notwithstanding, no devoted item that a man may devote unto the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field, shall be sold or redeemed; every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28). The verse is interpreted to mean that any dedicated item that is most holy, i.e., that was consecrated for the altar and then dedicated to the priests, that item should be for the Lord, and the priests are not entitled to it.

verse.he: אַךְ־כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כׇּל־חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ־קׇדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But of all that anyone owns, be it human or animal or land-holding, nothing that has been proscribed for GOD may be sold or redeemed; every proscribed thing is totally consecrated to GOD.

notes.he: שהיה מתחילה קדש לה' הוא ואין כח כהן חל עליו:
notes.en: Every dedicated item that is most holy: that was holy to the Lord from the outset, belongs to the Lord, and the priest’s claim does not take effect on it.

notes.he: לפום ריהטא דרב הונא סבר לה כרבנן דפליגי עליה דר' יהודה בן בתירא במסכת ערכין פרק המקדיש (ערכין דף כח:) דאמר ר' יהודה בן בתירא סתם חרמים לבדק הבית שנאמר כל חרם קדש קדשים לה' וחכמים אומרים סתם חרמים לכהנים מה ת"ל כל חרם קדש קדשים מלמד שחל על קדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים ולאותו תנא ניחא שפיר דרשא דרב הונא דהא דאמר מלמד שחל על קדשים היינו דווקא חרמים דלה' אבל לר' יהודה בן בתירא לא שייך למדרש הכי דהא לא מיירי כלל בהתפסה דהקדש עילוי. הרמ"ר:
notes.en: Every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord: at first glance, Rav Huna holds like the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in tractate Arakhin, chapter HaMakdish (Arakhin 28b). There Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance, as it is stated, “Every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord.” And the Rabbis say: unspecified dedications are for the priests; then what does the verse teach by “every dedicated item is most holy”? It teaches that a dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and on offerings of lesser sanctity. According to that tanna [the Rabbis], Rav Huna’s interpretation works well, since what he says, that it teaches that it takes effect on consecrated items, refers specifically to dedications that are “to the Lord.” But according to Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira one cannot interpret it this way, since [for him the verse] does not speak of association by a consecration of value at all. [So writes] HaRaMaR.

notes.dh: דאמר קרא כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה'
notes.he: ומשמע דכל חרם דמן קדשי מזבח אתי אם החרימו לה' יהא ולא לכהנים משום דאין יכול להתפיסן דאינן שלו הילכך לא עשה כלום [וקא דייק מדוקיא דברייתא הא קדשי מזבח שהתפיסן לחרמי כהנים תפסין לעילוי (לא) תפסי כדאמינא. ונותנן לכהנים תיובתא דרב הונא:
notes.en: As the verse states: “Every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord.” This implies that every dedication that comes from items consecrated for the altar, if he dedicated it, shall be to the Lord and not to the priests, because he cannot associate them, since they are not his; therefore he has done nothing. And it infers from the precise wording of the baraita: but items consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests take effect for the value, as I said, and he gives it to the priests. A refutation of Rav Huna.

messages.text:
With regard to items consecrated for Temple maintenance that one associated with another sanctity, whether with a consecration for the altar, whose sanctity is more stringent than consecration for Temple maintenance, or with a dedication to the priests, he has done nothing.
The reason is that one cannot remove the sanctity of an item consecrated for Temple maintenance, and he has no ownership of value in it. As for the benefit of discretion, i.e., the right to choose the priest that will receive the offering, this is not relevant to items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and therefore it cannot be suggested that his act of consecration was with regard to the benefit of discretion.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection to the statement of Rav Huna from a baraita:

notes.he: דגופייהו לא מיפקע מבדק הבית וטובת הנאה לא שייכא בהו:
notes.en: He has done nothing: because their body is not removed from Temple maintenance, and the benefit of discretion does not apply to them.

notes.dh: קדשי בדק הבית שהתפיסן בין לקדשי מזבח בין לחרמי כהנים לא עשה ולא כלום
notes.he: פירש"י דבשלמא קדשי מזבח יש בהן טובת הנאה כדמפרש במתניתין אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מה טובת הנאה יש בהן:
notes.en: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance that one associated, whether with items consecrated for the altar or with dedications to priests, he has done nothing: Rashi explained: granted, items consecrated for the altar have a benefit of discretion, as is explained in the mishna; but with items consecrated for Temple maintenance, what benefit of discretion is there in them?

messages.text:
Similarly, in the case of a dedication to priests that one associated with another sanctity, whether with a consecration for the altar or with a consecration for Temple maintenance, he has done nothing.
One does not have any rights to an item dedicated to the priests, not even the benefit of discretion, as the dedicated item must be given to the members of the priestly watch serving in the Temple at the time of its dedication.

notes.he: אין לו שום חלק בהם ואפי' טובת הנאה משום דאינו רשאי ליתנן אלא לכהן שבאותו משמר ואליבא דמאן דמקיש מטלטלין לחרמי קרקעות בערכין בפרק המקדיש (ערכין דף כח.):
notes.en: And similarly dedications to priests: he has no share in them at all, not even the benefit of discretion, because he may give them only to a priest of that [serving] watch; and [this is] according to the one who compares movable property to dedications of land, in Arakhin, in the chapter HaMakdish (Arakhin 28a).

notes.he: פירש"י דאין לו בהן טובת הנאה שצריך הוא ליתנו לכהן (בע"כ) שבאותו משמר ואפילו למאן דלא מקיש מטלטלין לקרקעות ה"מ מקדיש עכ"ל ואומר מורי דהך מילתא דמקיש מטלטלין לקרקעות בערכין בפרק המקדיש (ערכין דף כח.) אמר רב חסדא המחרים מטלטלין נותנן לכל כהן שירצה שנאמר כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה החרים שדותיו נותנן לכהן שבאותו משמר ופריך וליקוש מטלטלין לקרקעות ומשני ולאו תנאי היא דאיכא דמקיש ואיכא דלא מקיש ומה שפירש אפילו למאן דלא מקיש ה"מ במקדיש לא הבין רבי לשונו אלא נראה לפרש למורי (שי') בדהיה כהן והכא אתיא כמאן דלא מקיש:
notes.en: Dedications to priests that one associated, etc.: Rashi explained that he has no benefit of discretion in them, since he must give it to the priest of that watch; “and even according to the one who does not compare movable property to land, that applies to one who consecrates” — end of his words. [Our printed Rashi reads “according to the one who compares.”] And my teacher says: this matter of comparing movable property to land is in Arakhin, chapter HaMakdish (Arakhin 28a): Rav Ḥisda said: one who dedicates movable property gives it to any priest he wishes, as it is stated, “Every dedicated item in Israel shall be yours”; if he dedicated his fields, he gives them to the priest of that watch. And it asks: but let us compare movable property to land! And it answers: is it not a dispute of tanna’im, since there is one who compares and one who does not? As for what he explained, “even according to the one who does not compare, that applies to one who consecrates,” my teacher did not understand his wording. Rather, my teacher thinks it should be explained as a case where he was a priest, and here it follows the one who does not compare.

messages.text: Since the baraita teaches only that one may not associate with another sanctity items consecrated for Temple maintenance or dedications to priests, it may be inferred with regard to animals consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests, that what he did is done, i.e., it takes effect. If so, this baraita is apparently a conclusive refutation of the statement of Rav Huna.
messages.quote: consecrated for the altar, if one associated such objects of his vow with dedications for the priests

notes.he: דשייך בהו טובת הנאה מה שעשה עשוי ויהיב הטובת הנאה לכהן:
notes.en: But items consecrated for the altar: to which the benefit of discretion applies, what he did is done, and he gives the benefit of discretion to the priest.

messages.text: One cannot draw such an inference from the baraita, as it is possible that the tanna chose to discuss only those two instances while omitting the case of an animal consecrated for the altar.
messages.lead: The Gemara responds: Rav Huna could have said to you:

notes.he: לקדשי מזבח דלא תנייה בהדי הני:
notes.en: That he omitted it: items consecrated for the altar, which he did not teach together with these.

messages.text: And as for the fact that the tanna omitted this latter case, he omitted it due to this reason, that the halakha differs depending on the case: With regard to animals consecrated for the altar that one associated with a consecration for Temple maintenance, what he did is done, and he must pay the Temple treasury a consecration of value, but if he associated it with a dedication to priests, he has done nothing.

notes.he: כלומר על דבר זה שייריה ואם הקדישן לב"ה מה שעשה עשוי ויהיב הקדש עילוי אבל לחרמי כהנים לא דבהדיא מיעטיה קרא:
notes.en: He omitted it on account of this one: that is, on account of this matter he omitted it: if he consecrated them for Temple maintenance, what he did is done and he gives a consecration of value; but for dedications to priests, not, because the verse explicitly excluded it.

notes.he: כי שיירא לדוקיא דלא תנא בברייתא אחרא דוקיא שיירה הא קדשי מזבח שהתפיס לעילוי לקדשי בדק הבית תפסין אבל לא דייק כדאמרת לחרמי כהנים דלחרמי כהנים לא תפסי כדאמינא. אי הכי כיון דלא תפסי לחרמי כהנים ניתנייה בפירוש בברייתא גבי הנך דתני לא עשה כלום:
notes.en: Rav Huna could say to you: when he omitted the inference, not teaching it in the baraita, he omitted it for this inference: but items consecrated for the altar that one associated for their value with items consecrated for Temple maintenance take effect. But he did not mean the inference you drew, for dedications to priests, since for dedications to priests they do not take effect, as I said. If so, since they do not take effect for dedications to priests, let him teach it explicitly in the baraita alongside those of which it teaches “he has done nothing.”

messages.text: But if so, let the tanna teach explicitly that one who associates an animal consecrated for the altar with a dedication to the priests has done nothing, alongside these other cases of items consecrated for Temple maintenance and dedications to priests.
messages.quote: but if he associated it with a dedication to priests, he has done nothing

notes.he: ונימא קדשי מזבח שהתפיסן לחרמי כהנים לא עשה כלום:
notes.en: Let him teach it alongside these: and say, “Items consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests, he has done nothing.”

messages.text: The tanna teaches instances where there are two types of consecration with which the item cannot be associated, e.g., an item consecrated for Temple maintenance, which cannot be associated with either a consecration for the altar or a dedication to the priests. By contrast, the tanna does not teach a case where there are not two instances with which the item cannot be associated, i.e., an animal consecrated for the altar. Although an animal consecrated for the altar cannot be associated with a dedication to the priests, it can be associated with a consecration for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: דאינו יכול להתפיסן אפי' לאחד משתי קדושות:
notes.en: Two: that one cannot associate them even with one of the two sanctities.

notes.dh: לא תנא הנך דאית ביה תרתי קתני
notes.he: כגון בין לקדשי מזבח בין לקדשי בדק הבית לא עשה כלום אבל הא קדשי מזבח שהתפיסן לחרמי כהנים דליתה בתרתי לא קתני דלחרמי כהנים לא תפסי הא לקדשי בדק הבית תפסי הלכך לא קתני לה בברייתא:
notes.en: It teaches those in which there are two: for example, “whether with items consecrated for the altar or with items consecrated for Temple maintenance, he has done nothing.” But this case, items consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests, in which there are not two, it does not teach: for with dedications to priests they do not take effect, but with items consecrated for Temple maintenance they do take effect. Therefore it does not teach it in the baraita.

notes.he: ל"א דניתנהו בתרתי קתני והיינו הך:
notes.en: Another version: it teaches [the cases] that can be taught with two; and this amounts to the same thing.

messages.text: One may consecrate animals already consecrated for the altar by a consecration of their value, and one can dedicate them.
messages.lead: Another objection to the statement of Rav Huna, from that which we learned in the mishna:
messages.quote: But one may consecrate animals already consecrated for the altar by a consecration of their value

messages.text: What, is it not correct to say that when the mishna is referring to a consecration of their value, this is a consecration for Temple maintenance, and when it states that one dedicates them, this is referring to dedications to a priest? Evidently, one can associate an animal consecrated for the altar with a dedication to priests.

notes.he: מקדישין אותו לבדק הבית ומחרימים דקתני היינו לחרמי כהנים ויהיב לכהנים העילוי:
notes.en: Is it not a consecration of value: one consecrates it for Temple maintenance; and “one dedicates” that it teaches is for dedications to priests, and he gives the priests the value.

notes.he: מאי לאו הקדש עילוי לשם קדשי בדק הבית ויהיב עילויין לבדק הבית ומחרימין אותן ויהיב עילויין לחרמי כהנים:
notes.en: Is it not a consecration of value for the sake of items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and he gives their value to Temple maintenance; and “one dedicates them,” and he gives their value to the priests’ dedications?

messages.text: No, this is not the meaning of the mishna. Rather, both this and that are referring to consecrations for Temple maintenance. And the mishna is teaching that there is no difference whether he expresses a term of consecration, i.e., if he states: This animal is consecrated for Temple maintenance, in which case the animal is consecrated for Temple maintenance, and there is no difference if he expresses a term of dedication, i.e., he states: This animal is dedicated for Temple maintenance, as in this case too, the animal is consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: קדשי מזבח לבדק הבית בלשון הקדש ל"ש בלשון חרם יהיב העילוי לגזברין:
notes.en: There is no difference when he expresses: items consecrated for the altar [that he gives] to Temple maintenance, whether in a term of consecration or in a term of dedication, he gives the value to the treasurers.

notes.he: ומחרימין אותן נמי לצורך בדק הבית קאמר וקאמר (לו) דלא שנא כי מפיק להו קדשי מזבח בלשון הקדש דקאמר יהו חרם לבדק הבית תפסו לבדק הבית לעילוי:
notes.en: No, both this and that: “and one dedicates them” also speaks of the needs of Temple maintenance. And it says that there is no difference whether he expresses items consecrated for the altar in a term of consecration, or says, “Let them be a dedication for Temple maintenance”: they take effect for Temple maintenance, for the value.

messages.text: But this is not how it is taught in a baraita. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: both this and that are referring to consecrations for Temple maintenance

messages.text: One can consecrate animals consecrated for the altar by a consecration of its value, that is, a consecration for Temple maintenance, and one can dedicate them by a dedication to priests.

notes.he: כדמתרצת דקתני בהדיא ומחרימין אותן חרמי כהנים כלומר לכהנים והתניא כו':
notes.en: But it is not taught so in the baraita, as you answer, for it teaches explicitly “and one dedicates them: dedications to priests,” meaning to the priests. And isn’t it taught, etc.

messages.text: And furthermore, isn’t it taught in another baraita:
With regard to animals consecrated for the altar that one subsequently consecrated their value as dedications to the priests, what he did is done.
The refutation of the opinion of Rav Huna is a conclusive refutation.
But Rav Huna says a verse as the source for his opinion. Since his opinion is refuted, how should the verse be interpreted?
messages.quote: every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord

notes.he: דאמר כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה' יהא כלומר ולא לכהנים]:
notes.en: But Rav Huna states a verse: for he said, “Every dedicated item is most holy; it shall be to the Lord,” meaning, and not to the priests.

messages.text: That verse is not interpreted in the manner of Rav Huna. The verse states: “Notwithstanding, no dedicated item that a man may devote unto the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field, shall be sold or redeemed; every dedicated item is most holy unto the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28). The emphasis that “every dedicated item” is most holy indicates that a dedication to the priests takes effect on every item, even with regard to animals consecrated for the altar.

verse.he: אַךְ־כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כׇּל־חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ־קׇדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But of all that anyone owns, be it human or animal or land-holding, nothing that has been proscribed for GOD may be sold or redeemed; every proscribed thing is totally consecrated to GOD.

notes.he: קרא לא כרב הונא משמע מדהוה ליה למכתב חרם קדשי קדשים הוא וכתיב וכל חרם הכי משמע על הכל חייל חרם ואפילו אמידי דקדש קדשים הוא:
notes.en: Ulla said: the verse does not read like Rav Huna. It implies: since it could have written “A dedicated item is most holy,” and it writes “and every dedicated item,” it implies this: a dedication takes effect on everything, even on something that is most holy.

notes.he: קרא להכי אתא חרם כל חרם דיכיל למימר חרם מאי כל חרם מלמד שחל חרם על כל קדש וקדש בין על קדשי קדשים דלה' הם בין על קדשים קלים לעילוי כדאמרן:
notes.en: Ulla said: the verse comes for this: “dedicated item, every dedicated item.” Since it could have said “dedicated item,” what is “every dedicated item”? It teaches that a dedication takes effect on every single sacred item, whether on offerings of the most sacred order, which are the Lord’s, or on offerings of lesser sanctity, for the value, as we said.

messages.text: Since Ulla holds that animals consecrated for the altar may be associated with a dedication to priests, evidently he also holds that they may be associated with a consecration for Temple maintenance, as even Rav Huna agrees they may be associated with such a consecration. And did Ulla actually say this? But didn’t Ulla say that one who associates a burnt offering with a consecration for Temple maintenance has only the delay of
messages.quote: a dedication to the priests takes effect on every item, even with regard to animals consecrated for the altar

notes.dh: והאמר עולא המתפיס עולה לב"ה אין בה אלא עיכוב גזברין
notes.he: פירש רש"י שאינה קריבה עד שיבואו גזברין לעמוד על גבה כדאמר התם היאך קרבנו של אדם קרב ואינו עומד ע"ג אבל שום דמים לא יהיה לב"ה וכ"ש לחרמי כהנים דהא אפילו רב הונא דפליג אחרמי כהנים מודה בב"ה ומשני מדרבנן כלומר הך ברייתא דלעיל דשייריה לקדשי מזבח לומר דחיילי עליה בקדשי עילוי מדרבנן הוא דחייל דמדאורייתא ליכא אלא עיכוב גזברין ועולא נמי כי תירצה מדרבנן תירצה וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא ועיקר קרא לרבות חרמים למעילה כדכתיב בהו לה' עד כאן לשונו וקשיא טובא דאם כן תיקשי מתני' דלעיל דאמר מקדישין אותן הקדש עילוי ועוד קשה השתא אסיקנא דהוו דרבנן ובערכין (גם זה שם) דריש כל חרם לה' מלמד שחל על קדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים משמע דהוי עיקר דרשא לכן נראה לפרש דלעולא ודאי חייב ליתן הוא הדמים לבדק הבית כדתנן במתני' ומקדישין אותן הקדש עילוי וכן בערכין ועולא ה"ק אין בה אלא עיכוב גזברין כלומר אין להקדש בגוף הבהמה אלא שהגזברין יעכבו אותה לשוחטה עד שישומו אותה ומתחייב דמי שומא לב"ה ואשמעינן שאין הקדש חל על גופה של עולה [אלא] לענין שתאסר לשוחטה עד שיפדנה הלכך ממתני' ניחא ליה דלא קאמר במתני' שיחול על גוף הבהמה אלא בחוב בעלמא אבל קשיא ליה כיון דמ"מ עולה דיכול להתפיס לחרמי כהנים א"כ ע"כ ס"ל דהקדש חל על גוף הבהמה דאם לא כן על מה יחול חרם הכהן דלא דמי לחרמי בדק הבית שאם אמר הרי עלי מנה לבדק הבית חייב דאמירה לגבוה כמסירה להדיוט אבל חרמי כהנים ודאי אם אמר הרי עלי מנה לחרמי כהנים אם ירצה יחזור בו דאמירה להדיוט לאו כלום היא וחרמי כהנים לא הוו אלא כאומר חפץ זה לחרמי כהנים שאז ודאי החרמים חל על גוף החפץ א"כ ע"כ סבר עולא שהחרם חל על גוף הבהמה א"כ למה אין בה אלא עיכוב גזברין ואמאי הרי איכא איסורא לשחוט עד שיפדנה ומשני מדרבנן כלומר מדאורייתא אינו חל כלל על גוף הבהמה ומדרבנן הוא דחל על גוף הבהמה ואסור לשוחטה ועיקר קרא ודאי אתא לומר שחל על הקדש לכל הפחות להתחייב מטעם חוב ועוד מצא רבי בשם ר"י דפריך מעולא דאמר המתפיס עולה לב"ה ולא אמר לחרמי כהנים ש"מ דסבר דחרמי כהנים לא אמר כלום כרב הונא וקשיא למילתא דדריש דיכול להתפיס לחרמי כהנים ומשני מדרבנן היא דדריש מכל חרם דחרמי כהנים היינו מדרבנן:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi explains “only the delay of the treasurers” to mean the offering is not sacrificed until the treasurers come to stand over it (as “how can a person’s offering be sacrificed while he does not stand over it?”), but no monetary value goes to Temple maintenance, and all the more so not to the priests’ dedications, since even Rav Huna, who disputes regarding the priests’ dedications, agrees regarding Temple maintenance. And the answer “by rabbinic law” means that the earlier baraita, which omitted items consecrated for the altar so as to say a consecration of value takes effect on them, speaks of rabbinic law, since by Torah law there is only the treasurers’ delay; Ulla too answered by rabbinic law, the verse is mere support, and its main point is to include dedications in misuse, since it says of them “to the Lord.” Tosafot find this very difficult: (1) the mishna itself says “one may consecrate them by a consecration of value”; (2) Arakhin (28b) derives from “every dedicated item” that a dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and of lesser sanctity, which reads as a primary derivation. So they explain: according to Ulla he certainly must pay the value to Temple maintenance, as the mishna and Arakhin teach; “only the delay of the treasurers” means the Temple has nothing in the animal’s body except that the treasurers hold back its slaughter until it is appraised, and he owes the appraised value. The mishna is then no difficulty, since it says only that he owes a debt, not that the consecration takes effect on the body. The Gemara’s difficulty is rather this: since Ulla holds a burnt offering can be associated with the priests’ dedications, the dedication must take effect on the animal’s body. For a priest’s dedication is unlike Temple maintenance: “It is incumbent upon me to give a maneh to Temple maintenance” binds, since a statement to the Most High is like delivery to an ordinary person, but “It is incumbent upon me to give a maneh to the priests’ dedications” can be retracted, since a statement to an ordinary person is nothing; so it works only as “this object is a dedication,” on the object’s body. Then why only the treasurers’ delay, when slaughter is forbidden until redemption? The answer, “by rabbinic law”: by Torah law it does not take effect on the animal’s body at all; only by rabbinic law does it take effect on the body and forbid slaughter; and the verse’s main point is that it takes effect at least as a debt. Tosafot’s teacher also found in the name of the Ri: the question is from Ulla’s mentioning Temple maintenance and not the priests’ dedications, implying he holds like Rav Huna that the priests’ dedications are nothing, which contradicts his derivation that one can associate with them; and the answer is that his derivation from “every dedicated item” for the priests’ dedications is rabbinic. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: דחל עלייהו חרם על קדשי המזבח:
notes.en: And did Ulla say this: that a dedication takes effect on items consecrated for the altar?

notes.dh: ומי אמר עולא הכי והאמר עולא כו'
notes.he: אלמא לא תפס' קדושי מזבח לקדשי בדק הבית וכ"ש חרמים דלא תפסי:
notes.en: And did Ulla say this? But didn’t Ulla say, etc. Evidently, items consecrated for the altar are not taken by items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and all the more so dedications do not take effect.

messages.text: the treasurers alone preventing the offering from being sacrificed. In other words, the owner of an offering must stand over the animal when it is sacrificed, and in the case of a burnt offering that was associated with a consecration for Temple maintenance, the Temple treasurer is the owner. Evidently, Ulla maintains that the offering does not require an appraisal for a consecration of its value before it may be sacrificed, despite the fact that it was associated with a consecration for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: שאינה קריבה עד שיבואו הגזברין לעמוד על גבה כדאמרי' בעלמא (תענית דף כו.) היאך קרבנו של אדם קרב והוא אינו עומד ע"ג אבל שום דמים לא יהיב לבדק הבית וכ"ש לחרמי כהנים דהא אפילו רב הונא דהוה פליג אחרמי כהנים הוה מודה אבדק הבית:
notes.en: Treasurers: that it is not sacrificed until the treasurers come to stand over it, as we say elsewhere (Ta’anit 26a): How can a person’s offering be sacrificed while he does not stand over it? But he gives no monetary value to Temple maintenance, and all the more so not to dedications to priests, since even Rav Huna, who disagreed regarding dedications to priests, agreed regarding Temple maintenance.

notes.he: והאמר עולא המתפיס עולה לעילוי דבדק הבית אין בה אלא עיכוב גזבר בלבד כלומר (אם אינה צריכה) לא חל עליה כלום ואינה צריכה לא שום פדייה ולא שום המתנה אלא עיכוב גזבר בלבד כלומר לאלתר כשיבא הגזבר של הקדש יתן רשות לשוחטה וישחטוה לשם עולה מיד בלא פדייה. וכיון דקדושת בדק הבית לא חל עליה כ"ש דחרם נמי לא חל עליה דהא רב הונא דאית ליה דחל עליה קדשי בדק הבית קאמר דלחרמי כהנים לא תפסי וכ"ש עולא דאמר דלבדק הבית לא תפיס ק"ו דלחרמים נמי לא תפסי. וקשיא לעולא דאמר חרם כל חרם:
notes.en: But didn’t Ulla say: one who associates a burnt offering for the value of Temple maintenance has only the delay of the treasurer alone. That is, nothing takes effect on it, and it requires neither any redemption nor any waiting, only the delay of the treasurer alone: that is, as soon as the treasurer of the Temple comes, he gives permission to slaughter it, and they slaughter it as a burnt offering at once, without redemption. And since the sanctity of Temple maintenance does not take effect on it, all the more so a dedication does not take effect on it. For Rav Huna, who holds that the consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on it, says that they do not take effect for dedications to priests; all the more so Ulla, who says that it does not take effect for Temple maintenance, [must hold] a fortiori that they do not take effect for dedications either. And this is difficult for Ulla, who said “dedicated item, every dedicated item.”

notes.dh: וקדשי מזבח שהתפיסן לחרמי כהנים מי קרבינן
notes.he: (כדקאמר עולה שהתפיסן לקדשי בדק הבית אין בה אלא עיכוב גזבר וכ"ש חרמים) והא קרא קאמר עולא כל חרם קדש קדשים מלמד שחל על כל קדש וקדש:
notes.en: And items consecrated for the altar that one associated with dedications to priests: are they sacrificed? (As he says: a burnt offering that one associated with items consecrated for Temple maintenance has only the treasurer’s delay, and all the more so dedications.) But Ulla states a verse, “every dedicated item is most holy,” teaching that it takes effect on every single sacred item! [Like Rashi’s (rashi:b5.2), Rabbeinu Gershom’s text has a question “are they sacrificed?” that is not in our printed Gemara.]

messages.text: Actually, this halakha, that one who associates an animal consecrated for the altar with a consecration for Temple maintenance must give the value of the animal for Temple maintenance, was instituted by the Sages; by Torah law, there is only the delay attributed to the treasurers. This is also the opinion of Ulla.
messages.quote: one who associates a burnt offering with a consecration for Temple maintenance has only the delay

notes.he: האיך ברייתא דלעיל דשיירא לקדשי מזבח למימרא דחייל עלייהו הקדש עילוי מדרבנן הוא דחייל דמדאורייתא ליכא אלא עיכוב גזברין ועולא נמי כי תירצה מדרבנן תירצה וקרא לאסמכתא ועיקר קרא למעילה אתא לרבות חרמי כהנים למעילה והכי משמע כל החרם הוי לה' דאי איתהני מיניה פורתא מעל:
notes.en: And it answers, by rabbinic law: that earlier baraita, which omitted items consecrated for the altar, meaning that a consecration of value takes effect on them, [means that] it takes effect by rabbinic law, since by Torah law there is only the treasurers’ delay. And Ulla too, when he answered it, answered it by rabbinic law, and the verse is a mere support; the main point of the verse comes for misuse, to include dedications to priests in misuse. And this is its implication: every dedication is the Lord’s, so that if one derived even slight benefit from it, he has misused.

notes.he: אין מדאורייתא לא תפיס בהו חרם דהא המתפיס עולה לבדק הבית אין בה אלא עיכוב גזבר אלא מדרבנן קא אמינא דחל עליהו חרם וקרא דכתיב כל חרם למעילה הוא דאתא דמועלין בחרמין מריבוי דכל:
notes.en: Ulla could say to you: yes, by Torah law a dedication does not take effect on them, since one who associates a burnt offering with Temple maintenance has only the treasurer’s delay; but I spoke by rabbinic law, that a dedication takes effect on them. And the verse that writes “every dedicated item” comes for misuse: that one is liable for misuse of dedications, from the inclusion of “every.”

notes.he: מדרבנן הוא דתפסי חרמים קדשי מזבח:
notes.en: Ulla could say to you: it is by rabbinic law that dedications take effect on items consecrated for the altar.

messages.text: And as for the verse that Ulla cites as a source for the halakha that an animal consecrated for the altar can be associated with dedications to priests (Leviticus 27:28), it is mere support for this rabbinic law. The verse actually comes to teach that one is subject to the halakhot of misuse in the case of dedications to priests.

notes.he: לאו להכי אתא אלא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא ואלא קרא כל חרם למאי אתא מיבעי ליה כל למעילה דחרם כו':
notes.en: And this verse, “every dedicated item,” does not come for this; rather, it is a mere support. Then what does the verse “every dedicated item” come for? “Every” is needed for misuse of dedications, etc.

messages.text: If the term in the verse “every dedicated item” serves to teach only that one is subject to the halakhot of misuse in the case of dedications to priests, why does one need this verse at all? After all, an expression of most holy is written in the verse, as it states: “Is most holy unto the Lord,” and the halakhot of misuse apply to all sanctified items.
messages.quote: The verse actually comes to teach that one is subject to the halakhot of misuse

notes.he: ק"ק מדלא דרשינן כל חרם לומר דמיירי בחרמי כהנים אם כן קדשי קדשים בחרמי כהנים היכא כתיב ואומר מורי הרמ"ר דסמיך אקרא אחרינא דכתיב גבי חרמי כהנים (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״א) והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל קודש (קדשים) לה' כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו וקדש קדשים לאו דוקא אלא כלומר קדש לה' ומ"ו אומר דאפי' נמי לא דריש (כלל דרשי) כל לרבות חרמי כהנים מ"מ הוא יודע דפשטיה דקרא דקדש קדשים קאי לחרמי כהנים דכתיב בתריה לא יגאל ולא ימכר והיינו חרמי כהנים דאין להן פדיון דאילו חרמי בד"ה אדרבה כל עיקרן לפדיון קיימי ומיהו מ"מ היה צריך ייתור לרבות להקדש עילוי משדה קדש לה' דמשמע דממעט להו אבל לענין מעילה מפשטיה שמעינן:
notes.en: For misuse (“most holy” is written): this is somewhat difficult. Since we do not interpret “every dedicated item” to say that it speaks of dedications to priests, then where is “most holy” written regarding dedications to priests? My teacher HaRaMaR says that it relies on another verse written regarding dedications to priests: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy unto the Lord, as a field dedicated; the possession of it shall be the priest’s” (Leviticus 27:21); and “most holy” is not precise, but means “holy unto the Lord.” And my teacher says: even if it did not interpret “every” to include dedications to priests, he nevertheless knows that the plain meaning of the verse, “most holy,” refers to dedications to priests, since it is written after it, “shall be sold or redeemed,” and that means dedications to priests, which have no redemption, whereas dedications for Temple maintenance, on the contrary, stand entirely for redemption. Nevertheless, an extra word was needed to include the consecration of value, since “the field … holy unto the Lord” implies excluding them; but misuse we learn from its plain meaning.

notes.dh: למה לי קרא למעילה קדש קדשים כתיב
notes.he: אלמא דדינא כקדשי קדשים דמועלין בה:
notes.en: Why do I need a verse for misuse? “Most holy” is written. Evidently its law is like offerings of the most sacred order, for which one is liable for misuse.

messages.text: And according to your reasoning, that liability for misuse in the case of dedications to priests is derived from the term “is most holy,” then consider that which Rabbi Yannai said:
messages.quote: an expression of most holy is written in the verse

notes.dh: ולטעמיך הא דאמר ר' ינאי אין מעילה מפורשת כו'
notes.he: ל"א והא רב הונא קרא קאמר ההוא מיתבעי לכדתנן כו':
notes.en: And according to your reasoning, that which Rabbi Yannai said: misuse is explicit only, etc. Another version: “But Rav Huna states a verse!” That one is needed for that which we learned, etc.

messages.text: The halakhot of misuse are written explicitly in the Torah only in the case of one who misuses a burnt offering, as it is stated with regard to the guilt offering brought for misuse: “If anyone commit a trespass, and sin through error, in the holy items of the Lord” (Leviticus 5:15). The verse indicates only that one is liable for misuse of burnt offerings, which are exclusively for the Lord.

verse.he: נֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תִמְעֹל מַעַל וְחָטְאָה בִּשְׁגָגָה מִקׇּדְשֵׁי יְהֹוָה וְהֵבִיא אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ לַיהֹוָה אַיִל תָּמִים מִן־הַצֹּאן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף־שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל־הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְאָשָׁם׃
verse.en: When a person commits a trespass, being unwittingly remiss about any of GOD’s sacred things: They shall bring as a penalty to GOD a ram without blemish from the flock, convertible into payment in silver by the sanctuary weight, as a reparation offering.

messages.text: But the fact that the halakhot of misuse apply to a sin offering or a guilt offering, from which the priests or owners partake, is derived only from that which Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi taught.

The verse states at the conclusion of the passage discussing the sacrifice of a peace offering: “And the priest shall make them smoke upon the altar…all the fat is the Lord’s” (Leviticus 3:16). The word “all” serves to include the portions of offerings of lesser sanctity in the halakhot of misuse; all the more so is it the case that offerings of the most sacred order, e.g., a sin offering or guilt offering, are included.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

verse.he: וְהִקְטִירָם הַכֹּהֵן הַמִּזְבֵּחָה לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ כׇּל־חֵלֶב לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en:
The priest shall turn these into smoke on the altar as food, an offering by fire, of pleasing odor.
All fat is GOD’s.

notes.he:
דכתיב לה'. מההיא דרבי מפיק ר' ינאי נמי קדשי קדשים דכל חלב כתיב ורבי היינו טעמא דאמר קדשים קלים דלדידיה משמע ליה דחטאת ואשם בכלל קדשי ה' הואיל ואין לבעלים בהן כלום ולא איצטריך לרבויי אימורים ולר' ינאי מיהא איצטריך לרבויינהו ואע"ג דכתיב בין בחטאת בין באשם קדשי קדשים בצו את אהרן.
ל"א ירושלמי מנלן כלומר מאי משמע האי כל חרם דחייל אקדשי מזבח:
notes.en: To include the portions of offerings of lesser sanctity in misuse: since it is written “the Lord’s.” From that [teaching] of Rabbi, Rabbi Yannai derives offerings of the most sacred order as well, since “all the fat” is written. And the reason Rabbi said “offerings of lesser sanctity” is that, in his view, the sin offering and guilt offering are evidently included in “the holy items of the Lord,” since the owners have nothing in them, and there was no need to include [their] sacrificial portions; but according to Rabbi Yannai, at any rate, they needed to be included, even though “whether the sin offering or the guilt offering, it is most holy” is written [in the portion] “Command Aaron.” Another version, [marked] Yerushalmi: “From where do we derive it?” That is, what indicates that this “every dedicated item” takes effect on items consecrated for the altar?

notes.he: כלומר אם התפיסם לבדק הבית אמאי מקרבינהו להו בלא פדיון דקאמר אין בה אלא עיכוב גזברין והאי קרא כתיב לעיל כל חרם קדש דמשמע דחרם חייל אכל הקדש וקדש אסור לשחיטה ולהקרבה עד שתפדה הקדש בעילוי:
notes.en: Are they sacrificed: that is, if he associated them with Temple maintenance, why do we sacrifice them without redemption, as he says there is only the treasurers’ delay? But this verse written above, “every dedicated item is holy,” implies that a dedication takes effect on every single sacred item, and it is forbidden for slaughter and for sacrifice until it is redeemed for the Temple by a consecration of value. [This explains a question, “Are they sacrificed?”, that is not in our printed Gemara; Rabbeinu Gershom’s text has it too.]

messages.text: Why, then, do I need a verse to include these offerings? After all, an expression of “most holy,” is written with regard to a sin offering and guilt offering.

Rather, it must be that even though “most holy” is written with regard to them, nevertheless, a verse is required to include them in the halakhot of misuse. With regard to dedications as well, even though “most holy” is written with regard to them, a verse is required to include them in the halakhot of misuse.
One who consecrates a burnt offering for Temple maintenance has only the delay attributed to the treasurers alone preventing the offering from being sacrificed.
messages.lead: § The Gemara earlier cited a statement of Ulla with regard to one who associates a burnt offering with a consecration for Temple maintenance. The Gemara discusses the matter itself:

notes.dh: גופא [המקדיש עולה לב"ה] אין בה אלא עיכוב גזברין
notes.he: כלומר שומת הגזברין שיעכבו אותה מלשוחטה עד שישומו אותה ולא יוכלו לעכב לשחוט עד שיפד' דהקדש עילוי אינו אלא חוב מגזירת הכתוב:
notes.en: The matter itself: [one who consecrates a burnt offering for Temple maintenance] has only the delay of the treasurers: that is, the treasurers’ appraisal, that they hold it back from slaughter until they appraise it; but they cannot hold back the slaughter until it is redeemed, since the consecration of value is only a debt, by the decree of the verse.

messages.text: In the case of one who consecrates a burnt offering for Temple maintenance, it is prohibited to slaughter it until it is redeemed.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection to this opinion from a baraita:
messages.quote: One who consecrates a burnt offering for Temple maintenance

notes.dh: מיתיבי [המקדיש עולה לב"ה] אסור לשוחטה עד שתפדה
notes.he: שהחרם נתפס על גוף העולה ומשני מדרבנן הוא דאסור לשוחטה אבל ודאי מן התורה מתחייב הוא לשלם הדמים לב"ה ובפרק טבול יום (זבחים קג.) אמר לא מיבעיא למאן דאמר קדשי ב"ה מדאורייתא אלא אפילו למ"ד אין תפסי ה"מ בשר והשתא קשה טובא דהא מי איכא למ"ד קדשי ב"ה לא תפסי בהקדש עילוי ומתוך הלכה זו מיישבו רש"י לשם ופירש דלמ"ד תפסי היינו מקושיא דהכא דבעי לאוכוחי דאסור לשוחטו מן התורה אלא אפילו למ"ד לא תפסי היינו מהכא דמסיק היינו מדרבנן מכל מקום ה"מ בשר אבל עור תפיס ובעי פדייה:
notes.en: They raised an objection: [one who consecrates a burnt offering for Temple maintenance] is forbidden to slaughter it until it is redeemed: since the dedication takes hold on the body of the burnt offering. And it answers: it is by rabbinic law that slaughtering it is forbidden, but by Torah law he is certainly obligated to pay the value to Temple maintenance. And in the chapter Tevul Yom (Zevaḥim 103a) it says: it is not necessary [to say this] according to the one who says items consecrated for Temple maintenance [take effect] by Torah law; but even according to the one who says they do not take effect, that applies to the flesh. Now this is very difficult: is there anyone who says that items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not take effect by a consecration of value? And from this halakha Rashi settled it there, explaining that “according to the one who says they take effect” is from the question here, which seeks to prove that it is forbidden to slaughter it by Torah law, and “even according to the one who says they do not take effect” is from here, where it concludes that it is by rabbinic law; in any case, that applies to the flesh, but [the consecration] does take effect on the hide, and it requires redemption.

notes.dh: עולה שהתפיסה לקדשי בדק הבית אסורה לשוחטה עד שתפדה
notes.he: כדאמרן אם נדר נותן דמיהן ואם נדבה נותן טובתה. מאי אסורה עד שתפדה מדרבנן:
notes.en: A burnt offering that one associated with items consecrated for Temple maintenance is forbidden to slaughter until it is redeemed: as we said, if a vow, he gives their value, and if a gift-offering, he gives its benefit. What is “forbidden until it is redeemed”? By rabbinic law.

messages.text: This baraita is referring to the halakha by rabbinic law; by Torah law, a burnt offering cannot be consecrated by means of a consecration of value, and only the presence of the treasurers is required for it to be sacrificed.
messages.quote: prohibited to slaughter it until it is redeemed

messages.text: This too stands to reason, from the fact that the latter clause of the baraita teaches: If he transgressed and slaughtered it before redeeming it what he did is done and he is not required to redeem it. But if the burnt offering must be redeemed by Torah law, how can the baraita state that what he did is done? Evidently, the burnt offering is redeemed by rabbinic law.

notes.he: בלא פדייה מה שעשה עשוי:
notes.en: And if he transgressed and slaughtered it without redemption, what he did is done.

messages.text: Rather, what will you say? Will you say that the baraita is referring to the halakha by rabbinic law? If so, say the last clause of the baraita: And anyone who derives benefit from this burnt offering misuses consecrated property on two counts of misuse, one for deriving benefit from an animal consecrated for the altar and one for deriving benefit from an item consecrated for Temple maintenance.
But if the burnt offering is consecrated with a consecration of value by rabbinic law, why does one who derives benefit from this burnt offering misuse consecrated property on two counts of misuse?

notes.he: אחת משום קדשי מזבח ואחת משום קדשי ב"ה ואי מדרבנן הא לא חיילא קדושת ב"ה אלא מדרבנן:
notes.en: Two counts of misuse: one on account of items consecrated for the altar and one on account of items consecrated for Temple maintenance. And if it is by rabbinic law, the sanctity of Temple maintenance takes effect only by rabbinic law.

notes.he: וא"ת והא משכחת בכמה מקומות ומועלין מדרבנן גבי דם וביצי תורין (מעילה דף יב) וי"ל דה"מ במידי דלא בדילי מיניה אבל הכא בדילי כבר מחמת הקדש קמא:
notes.en: And if by rabbinic law, why two counts of misuse? And if you say: but we find in several places that one is liable for misuse by rabbinic law, regarding blood and the eggs of turtledoves (Me’ila 12)? One can say: that applies to something people do not keep away from, but here they already keep away from it on account of the first consecration.

notes.he: אי הכי אימא סיפא ומועלין בה אם נהנה ממנה או מגיזתה אם נהנה ממנה:
notes.en: If so, say the latter clause: and one is liable for misuse of it, if he derived benefit from it or from its shearings, if he derived benefit from it.

messages.text: This is what the baraita is saying: And if the consecration of value of this burnt offering was by Torah law, it is fit to be liable for misuse on two counts of misuse.

notes.he: אילו הויא קדושה בתרייתא מדאורייתא וראוי אי לאו (דמדר' בהוא) דהקדיש ולאו דאורייתא:
notes.en: Fit: had the latter sanctity been by Torah law; and it would be fit, were it not that his consecration [takes effect only by rabbinic law] and not by Torah law. [The printed wording of this comment is garbled.]

notes.dh: ב' מעילות אחד משום קדשי מזבח ואחד משום קדשי בדק הבית
notes.he: ואי מדרבנן אסורה אמאי ב' מעילות. אימא ראויה למעול בה ב' מעילות אילו מדאורייתא אסור אבל כיון דמדרבנן אין בה אלא מעילה אחת:
notes.en: Two counts of misuse: one on account of items consecrated for the altar and one on account of items consecrated for Temple maintenance. And if it is forbidden by rabbinic law, why two counts of misuse? Say: it is fit for one to be liable for two counts of misuse in it, had it been forbidden by Torah law; but since it is by rabbinic law, there is only one misuse in it.

messages.caption: Associating one sanctity with another: what the baraita rules, where Rav Huna was refuted, and what Ulla holds by Torah law.

messages.text: The mishna cites a dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis with regard to animals consecrated for the altar and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. The Rabbis hold that if they died and were not redeemed, they cannot be redeemed and they must be buried, whereas Rabbi Shimon maintains that this is the halakha only with regard to animals consecrated for the altar; animals consecrated for Temple maintenance can be redeemed.

notes.he: בעלי מומין אותן שאמר אחד קדשי מזבח כו':
notes.en: And if they died: blemished ones, those of which it said, “both items consecrated for the altar,” etc.

messages.text: According to the Rabbis, both animals consecrated for the altar and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, as it states in the Torah with regard to the redemption of consecrated animals: “And if it be any unclean animal, of which they may not bring an offering unto the Lord, then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad; as you the priest values it, so shall it be” (Leviticus 27:11–12). Any consecrated animal that cannot be stood before the priest, e.g., one that died, is not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and must be buried.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

notes.he: והאי אם מתו יקברו אכולהו קאי. ר"ש ורבנן תרוייהו ילפי טעמייהו מקרא לקמן בין אליבא דר' יוחנן בין אליבא דר"ל:
notes.en: Both items consecrated for the altar, etc.: and this “if they died they must be buried” refers to all of them. Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis both derive their reasons from a verse below, both according to Rabbi Yoḥanan and according to Reish Lakish.

notes.dh: א"ר יוחנן [לרבנן] אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי ב"ה היו בכלל העמדה והערכה
notes.he: ומתני' דאם מתו יקברו קאי גם אקדשי קדשים דסיפא ור"ש פליג ואמר קדשי ב"ה לא הוו [בכלל העמדה והערכה]:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: [according to the Rabbis,] both items consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in standing and valuation: and the mishna’s “if they died they must be buried” refers also to the offerings of the most sacred order [i.e., the altar offerings] of the latter clause. And Rabbi Shimon disagrees and says that items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included in standing and valuation].

notes.he: ר' שמעון אומר קדשי בדק הבית אם מתו יפדו אמר ר' יוחנן לרבנן דאמר אם מתו יקברו אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל העמדה והערכה הילכך כיון דמתו ואי אפשר למעבד להו העמדה והערכה לא יפדו אלא יקברו:
notes.en: They must be buried. Rabbi Shimon says: items consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, can be redeemed. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: according to the Rabbis, who say “if they died they must be buried,” both items consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in standing and valuation. Therefore, since they died and it is impossible to perform standing and valuation for them, they are not redeemed but buried.

messages.text: According to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, as that verse is discussing animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. Accordingly, if an animal consecrated for Temple maintenance died and was not redeemed, it must be buried without redemption. But animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation, as the verse is not referring to such animals. Accordingly, if they died they are redeemed.

notes.dh: ורשב"ל אמר [לרבנן] קדשי מזבח לא הוו קדשי ב"ה הוו
notes.he: ומתני' דאם מתו יקברו לא קאי אלא אקדשי ב"ה ואע"ג דתני בתחילת הבבא אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי ב"ה אין משנין אותם משמע דקאי כולה מתניתא אתרוייהו לא קשיא הא דהא ע"כ לא אכולה קאי דהא הקדש עילוי דלא קאי אלא אקדשי מזבח ור"ש פליג אדרבנן ואמר דאדרבה איפכא מסתברא דקדשי ב"ה לא היו וקדשי מזבח היו וסברות הפוכות זו מזו:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish said: [according to the Rabbis,] items consecrated for the altar were not, items consecrated for Temple maintenance were: and the mishna’s “if they died they must be buried” refers only to items consecrated for Temple maintenance. And even though it teaches at the start of the clause, “both items consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance, one may not alter them,” which implies that the whole mishna refers to both, this is not difficult, since necessarily not all of it refers [to both]: the consecration of value refers only to items consecrated for the altar. And Rabbi Shimon disagrees with the Rabbis and says that, on the contrary, the reverse is reasonable: items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included], and items consecrated for the altar were; and these are lines of reasoning opposite to each other.

notes.he: וריש לקיש אמר לרבנן קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל העמדה ועליה קאמרי ואם מתו יקברו וזה וזה מודין בין ר' יוחנן בין ריש לקיש דלרבי שמעון קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה קדשי בדק הבית לא היו דהא לא קאמר ר' שמעון בפירוש דיפדו אלא קדשי בדק הבית בלבד ודברי הכל בין רבנן בין ר' שמעון בין ר' יוחנן ובין ריש לקיש דבעל מום מעיקרא אם מת דיפדו דלא היה בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish said: according to the Rabbis, items consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in standing, and about them they say “if they died they must be buried.” And this one and that one agree, both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, that according to Rabbi Shimon items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation [and] items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not, since Rabbi Shimon says explicitly that only items consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed. And everyone agrees, the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, that one blemished from the outset, if it died, is redeemed, since it was not included in standing and valuation.

messages.text: And both this one and that one, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, agree that according to Rabbi Shimon, animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation, and therefore if they died they are redeemed; and animals consecrated for the altar were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, and if they died they are not redeemed.

notes.he: רבי יוחנן ור"ל מודין דלר"ש קדשי בדק הבית לא היו אבל קדשי מזבח היו מדקתני קדשי בדק הבית יפדו ולא אמר סתמא יפדו מכלל דדווקא קאמר:
notes.en: This one and that one: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish agree that according to Rabbi Shimon items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included], but items consecrated for the altar were, since it teaches “items consecrated for Temple maintenance can be redeemed” and does not say simply “can be redeemed”; by implication, he spoke specifically.

messages.text: And according to both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, everyone agrees, both the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon, that if one consecrated for the altar an animal that was blemished from the outset, the animal was not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and it may be redeemed if it died.

notes.he: ועוד שניהם מודין דלדברי הכל בין לרבי שמעון בין לרבנן בעל מום מעיקרו לא הוה בהעמדה והערכה בקדשי מזבח כדמפרש טעמא לקמן ובקדשי ב"ה לא מיירי מידי דבעל מום מעיקרו דמודו דלרבנן קדשי בדק הבית בעו העמדה והערכה לא שנא בעל מום אחר הקדש ולא שנא קדם מומו להקדשו בעי העמדה והערכה דבקדשי ב"ה לא שאני לן בין בעל מום מעיקרא לתם ונעשה בעל מום שהרי על עצים ואבנים הן חלין:
notes.en: And everyone agrees: and furthermore both agree that according to everyone, both Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis, one blemished from the outset was not in [the halakha of] standing and valuation, with items consecrated for the altar, as the reason is explained below. And with items consecrated for Temple maintenance it does not speak of anything blemished from the outset, for they agree that according to the Rabbis items consecrated for Temple maintenance require standing and valuation, whether it became blemished after the consecration or its blemish preceded its consecration; for with items consecrated for Temple maintenance we do not distinguish between one blemished from the outset and an unblemished one that became blemished, since [that consecration] takes effect even on wood and stones.

notes.dh: ודברי הכל בעל מום מעיקרו לא היה
notes.he: ודוקא בקדשי מזבח אבל בקדשי ב"ה אפילו למאן דאית ליה הרי אין חילוק בין תם לבעל מום מעיקרו והכי מוכח כל הסוגיא:
notes.en: And everyone agrees that one blemished from the outset was not [included]: and this is specifically with items consecrated for the altar; but with items consecrated for Temple maintenance, even according to the one who holds [they were included], there is no distinction between an unblemished one and one blemished from the outset; and so the whole passage proves.

messages.caption: Standing and valuation: which consecrated animals were included, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, and what happens if they died.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna: Rabbi Shimon says that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died can be redeemed.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection to the explanation of Reish Lakish:
messages.quote: if animals consecrated for Temple maintenance died, they can be redeemed

messages.text: Granted, according to the explanation of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that according to the Rabbis, both this and that, i.e., animals consecrated for the altar and for Temple maintenance, were included in the halakha of standing and valuation and if they died they are not redeemed; this is why it was necessary for Rabbi Shimon to explain that specifically in the case of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died, they can be redeemed. This serves to emphasize that Rabbi Shimon disagrees with the Rabbis only with regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, not those consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: דאי הוה אמר סתמא יפדו כיון דתנא קמא בתרוייהו איירי הוי משמע דאתרוייהו פליג להכי פריש:
notes.en: This is why Rabbi Shimon needed to explain: for had he said simply “can be redeemed,” since the first tanna spoke of both, it would have implied that he disputes regarding both; therefore he explained.

messages.text: But according to the explanation of Reish Lakish, that the Rabbis hold that only animals consecrated for Temple maintenance may not be redeemed if they died, why must Rabbi Shimon explain that he is referring to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance? Let him say simply: If they died they can be redeemed, and it would be obvious that he is speaking of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, for if he were referring to animals consecrated for the altar, even the Rabbis agree that they may be redeemed.

notes.he: דאמר רבנן לא קיימי אלא אקדשי ב"ה:
notes.en: But according to Reish Lakish: who said that the Rabbis refer only to items consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: לר"ש לפרושי:
notes.en: Why must he: Rabbi Shimon explain?

notes.he: סתמא ואנא ידענא דלא קאי אלא אב"ה דהא בקדשי מזבח לא איירי כלל לעיל לא בפדייה ולא בקבורה:
notes.en: Let him say: simply, and I would know that he refers only to Temple maintenance, since regarding items consecrated for the altar [the first tanna] spoke above of nothing at all, neither of redemption nor of burial.

notes.he: דאמר דרבנן לא איירי כלל בקדשי מזבח דלא היו בכלל העמדה [והערכה] ואם מתו יפדו [מיבעי ליה] קצת קשה מנא ליה דילמא מיירי בקדשי מזבח וטעמא דאין פודין הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים:
notes.en: But according to Reish Lakish: who says that the Rabbis do not speak of items consecrated for the altar at all, since they were not included in standing [and valuation], and if they died they [should] be redeemed. It is somewhat difficult: from where does he know this? Perhaps it speaks of items consecrated for the altar, and the reason is that one does not redeem consecrated animals to feed them to the dogs.

notes.he: [אלא לריש לקיש דאמר דלרבנן קדשי בדק הבית היו ועליהו קאמרי יקברו למה ליה לר' שמעון לפרושי. לר' שמעון קדשי בדק הבית אם מתו יפדו. לימא אם מתו יפדו ואנן ידעינן דאמאי דקאמרי רבנן קא מהדר ר' שמעון:
notes.en: But according to Reish Lakish, who said that according to the Rabbis items consecrated for Temple maintenance were included and about them they say “they must be buried,” why must Rabbi Shimon explain, “items consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, can be redeemed”? Let him say “if they died they can be redeemed,” and we would know that Rabbi Shimon is responding to what the Rabbis said.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon did not know what the first tanna said, i.e., he was unsure whether the statement of the first tanna, the Rabbis, that the animal must be buried without redemption, is referring to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance or to animals consecrated for the altar.
messages.quote: Let him say simply: If they died they can be redeemed

notes.he: דמתני' לא הוה ידע מאי קאמרי רבנן וסבר דרבנן אתרוייהו קיימי:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon: of the mishna did not know what the Rabbis were saying, and thought that the Rabbis refer to both.

messages.text: And therefore, this is what Rabbi Shimon is saying to the first tanna: If your statement is referring to animals consecrated for the altar, that they are included in the halakha of standing and valuation and must be buried if they died without redemption, then I concede to you. By contrast, if your statement is referring to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, then I disagree with you and rule that if they died they can be redeemed.

notes.he: ר' שמעון לא הוה ידע על מאי אמרי רבנן יקברו והכי קאמר להו אי בקדשי מזבח תנן אם מתו יקברו כו'. (בסוגיא דת"ק) תניא כותיה דר' יוחנן כדקאמר לרבנן אחד זה ואחד זה היו בכלל העמדה והערכה] ואם כל בהמה טמאה וגו' והעמיד את הבהמה לפני הכהן דבעי העמדה והערכה בין קדשי מזבח ובין קדשי בדק הבית דבעלי מומין קבועין היינו שהיו קדשי מזבח ובהמה טמאה ממש היינו קדשי בדק הבית דאינה קדושה אלא לדמיה וכתי' בתרוייהו העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: Reish Lakish could say to you: Rabbi Shimon did not know about what the Rabbis said “they must be buried,” and this is what he says to them: if regarding items consecrated for the altar we learned “if they died they must be buried,” etc. It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, as he says that according to the Rabbis both this and that were included in standing and valuation: “And if it be any non-kosher animal,” etc., “then he shall set the animal before the priest,” which requires standing and valuation both for items consecrated for the altar and for items consecrated for Temple maintenance. For the permanently blemished ones are items consecrated for the altar, and the actual non-kosher animal is items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which is consecrated only for its value; and standing and valuation is written regarding both.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
messages.quote: both animals consecrated for the altar and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included

messages.text: The verse states: “And if it be any non-kosher animal, of which they may not bring an offering unto the Lord, then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it” (Leviticus 27:11–12). The Sages teach that the verse is speaking of blemished animals, that they can be redeemed. The verse indicates that one redeems a blemished animal by means of standing and valuation.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

notes.he: ל"א מדקתני וכולהו כלישנא קמא:
notes.en: Another version: “from the fact that it teaches,” and all of it as in the first version.

messages.text: Do you say that the verse is speaking of blemished animals; or perhaps it is referring only to a non-kosher animal, and it is teaching that a non-kosher animal that was consecrated for Temple maintenance is redeemed through standing and valuation?

When it says later in that passage: “And if it be of a non-kosher animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:27), a non-kosher animal is thereby stated as subject to redemption.

verse.he: וְאִם בַּבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁתוֹ עָלָיו וְאִם־לֹא יִגָּאֵל וְנִמְכַּר בְּעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if it is of impure animals, it may be ransomed at its assessment, with one-fifth added; if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessment.

messages.text: Continues on 33a: the baraita asks how, then, to understand “And if it be any non-kosher animal, of which they may not bring an offering,” and answers that it speaks of blemished animals, which can be redeemed.
